key_insight: ACCESS decouples finding strong candidate solutions from checking feasibility, using many cheap single-scenario solves plus large-scale batched simulation instead of expensive all-at-once scenario optimization.
engineering_relevance: This can make chance-constrained optimization practical for large stochastic design and operations problems by improving solution quality while reducing compute and leveraging GPU-parallel feasibility testing.
method: Generate candidate solutions from many inexpensive single-scenario subproblems rather than embedding all scenarios in one high-dimensional solve.
Evaluate feasibility separately with massive batched Monte Carlo simulation, which is highly parallel on GPUs.
Focus search on a 2D tradeoff space of conservatism and scenario diversity, with ACCESS(δ) adding probabilistic feasibility certification.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmark classes and five scenario distributions, ACCESS matched or exceeded the best objective in nearly every setting, while ACCESS(δ) was empirically feasible on every instance and SAA was often infeasible and much slower on harder cases.
watch_item: The approach relies on simulation-based feasibility assessment and tuning of conservatism/diversity, so certification and performance may depend on sampling budget, distribution shift, and problem structure.
paper_title: Optimization for One, Feasibility for Most: Decoupling Optimization from Feasibility in Chance-Constrained Programs
